chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: White musicians studied; advice to take lessons
summary: Jackson credits white musicians for studying hard and advises kids to learn technique so they can play with any feeling.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: And I give the white musicians a lot of credit because the white musicians really studied. He knew he had to study. He practiced a lot, he practiced a lot, where we used to go and just play. We had so much joy playing and we had so much originality and so much feeling that we didn't really, a lot of us, until later years we didn't take lessons, to practice like the white musicians did, you see.

And that's the reason I tell kids today, please study your instrument and learn all the technicalities of playing your instrument so that whatever you want to do and whichever feeling you want to play with, you have got it under your fingers, you've got your instrument under your fingers to do anything that you want to. You don't have to practice every day to think that you'll become stiff. That's not it. You practice on your instrument and take lessons so that you have control over your instrument at all times so that you can do what you want to and play with any feeling you feel like, if you have your instrument under your fingers.
Amen, Butter, I agree to that so much.
